rows.label: A new covenant; the first covenant, the old covenant
rows.note: The text's own phrases: “a new covenant” in the Hebrew (Jer 31:31) and in the Greek that quotes it (Heb 8:8, 9:15, 12:24), in the words over the cup (Luke 22:20; 1 Cor 11:25) and in Paul's ministry (2 Cor 3:6); and “the first covenant” (Heb 9:15) and “the old covenant” (2 Cor 3:14). In Heb 8:7, 8:13, 9:1 and 9:18 the Berean prints “covenant” where the Greek says only “the first” or “new” and has no noun, so those verses are not counted in this hub; Heb 8:13 is among its key verses. The Hebrew text says “a new covenant” only at Jer 31:31; “the old covenant” (2 Cor 3:14) and “the first covenant” (Heb 9:15) are phrases of Paul and of Hebrews, not of the Hebrew Scriptures. Jer 31:31-33 also stands in the rows on Egypt, Israel, the law, the heart, and making and breaking the covenant, so the passage can be read in sequence. How the new covenant stands to the covenants before it -- one covenant renewed, or another -- and to whom it is made, Israel or the church, is a point on which Christian traditions part, and the page takes no side. This row and the rows beside it are listed in the alphabetical order of their labels and carry no ranking.
